domain_label: Instructional Media & 3D Flashcard Producer — Pedagogical Image Generation for Cards
purpose: A method for PRODUCING teaching images for flashcards — image-occlusion source images, labeled anatomical diagrams, and mechanism flowcharts — generated through the extint-owned Codex MCP bridge under prompt discipline for anatomical/clinical accuracy, filtered by quality bands and a mandatory human clinical-correctness gate, and organized around the owner's 3-images-per-concept pattern (front/back/side views or story frames), with every generated asset carried honestly as machine-made and never shipped as clinical truth without human sign-off.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every design-quality threshold is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited recon and multimedia-learning literature
the generation transport is the Codex MCP bridge owned by the extint specialist; this KB decides WHAT image to make and HOW to verify it, not how extint wires the MCP server
the exact image-generation model reachable behind the Codex MCP bridge is not documented in the recon and is carried as a named UNKNOWN with a METHOD to resolve, never fabricated
the 3D pipeline (image -> Tripo -> GLB -> <model-viewer>) is a neighboring KB in this same specialist; this KB owns only the 2D image side and the multiview hand-off point into that pipeline
image occlusion itself (masking regions, authoring occlusion cards) is owned by the contenteng specialist; this KB only PRODUCES the source images it consumes
exclusions: the image -> Tripo -> GLB -> in-browser <model-viewer> 3D asset pipeline and the when-3D-helps-vs-decoration decision (neighboring media KB) beyond naming the multiview hand-off point
the image-occlusion authoring mechanics — mask-region selection, cloze-over-image card templates (owned by contenteng) — beyond specifying what makes a good source image to feed them
the Codex MCP bridge implementation, MCP server wiring, secrets and endpoint auth (owned by extint) beyond naming it as the generation transport
the knowledge-graph data model, terminology linking and semantic-zoom rendering (kgraph/viz specialists) even though generated diagrams may depict graph structure
spaced-repetition scheduling, item psychometrics and answer grading (sched/qcraft/voice) — this KB stops at delivering a verified image asset

glossary.definition: The coherence distinction: a pedagogical image carries structure or process information the card text cannot cheaply carry (a labeled diagram, an occlusion source, a mechanism flow), while a decorative image only adorns the card and, by multimedia-learning theory, adds extraneous load without teaching value and is rejected.

A base image PRODUCED by this KB for the contenteng specialist to turn into an image-occlusion card: it must have clearly separable, individually maskable regions, high contrast, and labels that can each be hidden and recalled — this KB makes it, contenteng masks it.

An anatomical or structural illustration with text labels attached to parts via leader lines, governed by the spatial-contiguity principle (label near its referent) and by clinical-accuracy constraints on the number, shape and arrangement of the depicted structures.

A directional diagram of a process (e.g. a metabolic pathway or a clinical decision) drawn as discrete steps connected by arrows showing causal or temporal flow, governed by the segmenting principle so each step is a distinct, chunked unit.

The image-generation transport owned by the extint specialist: OpenAI Codex can run as an MCP server over stdio (codex mcp-server) exposing itself to other agents, and this KB reaches the generator through that bridge; the specific image model behind it is not documented in the recon and is carried as a named UNKNOWN. [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §5 for the MCP-server mechanics]

The owner's requested convention of producing three images for each concept: either three spatial VIEWS (front / back / side) of a structure, or three sequential STORY FRAMES of a process; the view variant doubles as the multiview input the 3D pipeline can consume.

The point where front/back/side images leave this KB for the neighboring 3D KB: Tripo's multiview_to_model accepts 2-4 reference images with FRONT required and back/left/right optional, and its GLB output renders in-browser via Google's <model-viewer>. [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]

A discrete grade (A ship-ready, B fixable-by-re-prompt, C reject) assigned to a generated image on legibility, label correctness and anatomical accuracy, used to route it to ship, regenerate, or discard before the clinical gate.

The mandatory human sign-off on anatomical/clinical accuracy before any anatomy image is attached to a shippable card: generated images are treated as untrusted for clinical truth, so a human verifies structure identity and arrangement, and unverified anatomy never ships.

The class of errors a generative image model introduces — wrong number of structures, fused or duplicated anatomy, anatomically impossible arrangements, and garbled or invented label text — which is precisely why the clinical gate exists and why generated media is never trusted as clinical truth.

This KB owns the 2D slice of that gap — generating pedagogical images for cards (image-occlusion source images, labeled diagrams, mechanism flowcharts). Generation runs through the Codex MCP bridge owned by the extint specialist [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §5], and the image -> Tripo -> GLB -> <model-viewer> 3D flashcard pipeline is a NEIGHBORING KB in this same specialist that this KB only feeds at the multiview hand-off. The scope boundary is deliberate: decide WHAT teaching image to make and HOW to verify it, not how contenteng masks it, how extint wires MCP, or how the 3D pipeline meshes it.

this KB's 2D image-generation scope
the extint-owned Codex bridge as transport and the 3D KB as neighbor

pros.example: producing a maskable labeled diagram and handing it to contenteng rather than also building the occlusion card template

nodes.definition: Fix the first filter every candidate image passes: does it TEACH or merely DECORATE. By the multimedia coherence principle, adding material that does not serve the learning goal increases extraneous cognitive load and can hurt learning, so an image earns a place on a card only if it carries structure or process information the card text cannot cheaply carry [ESTIMATE — Mayer's cognitive theory of multimedia learning; to source-verify in this specialist's L1 research pass]. Operationally: a labeled diagram of a nerve's branches teaches; a stock photo of a smiling dentist decorates and is rejected. This gate is applied BEFORE any generation is requested, so decorative prompts are never even sent to the Codex bridge, saving generation cost and keeping cards clean.

included: the teaches-vs-decorates coherence test
rejecting decorative imagery before generation
the extraneous-load rationale
excluded: the specific principles for how a teaching image is laid out (their own node)
the quality banding of an already-generated image

pros.claim: A coherence gate up front prevents decorative bloat and wasted generation calls
pros.example: declining to generate a mood photo for a pharmacology card that a text mnemonic covers

cons.claim: The teaches-vs-decorates line is a judgment that can be drawn too strictly and drop a helpful orienting image
cons.example: rejecting a simple overview illustration that would have oriented a beginner

failure_modes: shipping decorative images that add load without teaching
over-pruning and removing genuinely orienting visuals
acceptance_tests: the gate states the coherence test, rejects decorative imagery before generation, and cites the extraneous-load rationale tagged ESTIMATE
revisit_triggers: learners report images as noise or as missing
the coherence threshold is re-tuned
the source-verify pass updates the multimedia citation

base.update_signal: learner feedback or a re-verified coherence citation changes the gate

nodes.definition: Enumerate the roles a generated card image can play, because each has different production demands. Three pedagogical roles: (1) image-occlusion SOURCE images — a base picture with separable, maskable regions that contenteng turns into hide-and-recall cards; (2) labeled DIAGRAMS — anatomical or structural illustrations with leader-line labels for identify-the-part recall; (3) mechanism FLOWCHARTS — directional step-and-arrow diagrams of a process or decision [FACT — these three roles follow directly from the app's card types: image occlusion, basic, and cloze per SPECIALIST_RECON; the pedagogical framing is ESTIMATE]. The role is chosen from the card's learning objective and drives every downstream choice — layout, label density, maskability, and whether the 3-image pattern uses views or story frames.

included: the occlusion-source / labeled-diagram / mechanism-flowchart roles
how the card objective selects the role
that the role drives layout and maskability
excluded: the layout rules per role (their own nodes)
decorative images (already excluded by the coherence gate)

pros.claim: A fixed role taxonomy makes every downstream production choice deterministic from the card objective
pros.example: an identify-the-structure objective selecting the occlusion-source role and its maskability requirements

cons.claim: Real objectives can blend roles, so a single image may be forced into one bucket it only partly fits
cons.example: a labeled diagram that is also meant to be occluded needing both label clarity and maskable regions

failure_modes: mis-selecting the role and producing an image the card type cannot use
forcing a blended objective into one role and losing part of its value
acceptance_tests: the taxonomy lists the three roles, ties role selection to the card objective, and states the role drives layout and maskability
revisit_triggers: a new card type is added to the app
objectives routinely blend two roles

base.update_signal: a new card type or a recurring blended objective changes the taxonomy

nodes.definition: State the multimedia-learning principles that constrain how a teaching image is designed, not just whether it teaches. The load-bearing ones for cards: SIGNALING (cue the to-be-learned element so attention lands on it), SPATIAL CONTIGUITY (place a label next to its referent, not in a distant legend), REDUNDANCY (do not duplicate the same text both as a spoken/on-card caption and as dense in-image prose), and SEGMENTING (break a process into discrete chunked steps) [ESTIMATE — Mayer's cognitive theory of multimedia learning design principles; to source-verify in this specialist's L1 research pass]. These convert directly into prompt and layout rules downstream: signaling becomes 'highlight structure X', spatial contiguity becomes 'labels adjacent to parts', segmenting becomes 'one step per frame'.

included: signaling, spatial contiguity, redundancy and segmenting as image-design constraints
how each maps to a prompt/layout rule
excluded: the concrete diagram and flowchart layouts (downstream nodes)

pros.claim: Grounding image design in named principles gives objective, teachable layout rules instead of taste
pros.example: rejecting a diagram whose labels sit in a distant legend for violating spatial contiguity

cons.claim: The principles are drawn from general multimedia research not yet source-verified here, so specific thresholds are provisional
cons.example: assuming a segmenting chunk size that a re-verified source might refine

failure_modes: citing the principles without translating them into concrete prompt/layout rules
over-signaling so every element is highlighted and none stands out
acceptance_tests: the node names signaling, spatial contiguity, redundancy and segmenting, maps each to a prompt/layout rule, and tags the set ESTIMATE to source-verify
revisit_triggers: the L1 source-verify pass updates a principle
a layout rule derived here fails in practice
a new principle is adopted

base.update_signal: a source-verified principle update or a failed layout rule changes the set

nodes.definition: Specify how to design a labeled diagram so it reads correctly. Labels must be legible at card render size, attached to their referent by a short leader line (spatial contiguity), limited in number so no single diagram is over-labeled, and drawn in a consistent visual register across the deck. Because generative models mangle small text, prefer generating the unlabeled illustration and overlaying labels deterministically where feasible, or explicitly constraining the prompt to few, large, correctly-spelled labels and verifying every one [ESTIMATE — design synthesis from the multimedia principles; the text-mangling tendency of image generators is a known SIGNAL]. The diagram's structures must satisfy the anatomical-accuracy constraints defined downstream before any label is trusted.

included: label legibility, leader-line contiguity, label-count limits
preferring overlaid or tightly-constrained labels over free-generated text
deferring structure accuracy to the anatomy-constraints node

pros.claim: Explicit label rules plus deterministic overlay dodge the generator's worst weakness — garbled small text
pros.example: generating a clean unlabeled molar illustration then overlaying crisp cusp labels programmatically

cons.claim: Deterministic overlay needs known label coordinates, which a free-form generation does not provide
cons.example: no reliable anchor point to place a 'lingual cusp' label on a generated tooth image

failure_modes: trusting free-generated in-image label text that is misspelled or misplaced
over-labeling a diagram until it is unreadable at card size
acceptance_tests: the node gives label-legibility, leader-line contiguity and count limits, prefers overlay or constrained labels, and defers structure accuracy to the anatomy node
revisit_triggers: the generator's text rendering materially improves
labels overflow at card render size
a deterministic overlay tool becomes available

base.update_signal: improved text rendering or an overlay tool changes the labeling approach

nodes.definition: Specify how to design a mechanism flowchart — a process or clinical-decision diagram. Draw discrete, chunked steps (segmenting) connected by directional arrows that make causal or temporal order unambiguous, with a single clear reading direction (top-to-bottom or left-to-right), minimal branching per view, and node text short enough to stay legible. For anything with real branching logic, prefer a deterministic diagram renderer (boxes-and-arrows from a text spec) over a generative image, because generators cannot be trusted to keep arrows connected to the right nodes or to spell step text correctly [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; generator unreliability on structured text is a SIGNAL]. The steps' clinical content is still subject to the human correctness gate downstream.

included: discrete chunked steps, directional arrows, single reading direction
preferring a deterministic diagram renderer for branching logic
short legible node text
excluded: the clinical correctness of the steps (gate node)

pros.claim: Deterministic box-and-arrow rendering for branching logic sidesteps the generator's structural unreliability
pros.example: rendering a caries-management decision tree from a text spec instead of an AI image with broken arrows

cons.claim: A deterministic renderer produces plainer visuals that may look less engaging than a generated illustration
cons.example: a stark boxes-and-arrows chart where an illustrated pathway would have drawn the eye

failure_modes: generating a flowchart whose arrows connect the wrong nodes
cramming a branching process into one over-dense view
acceptance_tests: the node gives discrete steps, directional arrows and one reading direction, prefers a deterministic renderer for branching, and defers step correctness to the gate
revisit_triggers: a flowchart's arrows are found mis-wired
a deterministic diagram renderer is adopted
branching processes routinely overflow one view

base.update_signal: a mis-wired flowchart or a renderer adoption changes the approach

nodes.definition: Specify what makes a good SOURCE image for an image-occlusion card, since contenteng consumes but does not produce it. The source needs clearly separable, individually maskable regions (distinct structures that can each be hidden and recalled), high figure-ground contrast so a mask reads cleanly, labels or landmarks that can be occluded one at a time, and enough resolution that a masked region stays legible when revealed [FACT — image occlusion consumes images in contenteng, this KB owns producing them, per SPECIALIST_RECON gap 4; the region/contrast requirements are ESTIMATE design synthesis]. The produced image is handed to contenteng which owns the mask-region selection and the occlusion card template — this KB stops at delivering a maskable, verified base image.

the hand-off to contenteng which owns masking
excluded: contenteng's mask-region selection and card template
the labeled-diagram labeling rules (sibling node) beyond maskability

pros.claim: Designing for maskability up front lets contenteng build clean occlusion cards without reworking the image
pros.example: a numbered anatomical plate whose each number can be individually hidden and asked

cons.claim: Maximizing separable regions can pull toward busy images that fight the coherence and legibility limits
cons.example: an overcrowded plate with twenty maskable structures that is unreadable at card size

failure_modes: producing a low-contrast image whose masks are ambiguous
delivering a source with regions too fused to mask individually
acceptance_tests: the node requires separable maskable regions, high contrast, individually occludable labels and adequate resolution, and hands masking to contenteng
revisit_triggers: contenteng reports source images it cannot mask cleanly

Images are requested through the Codex MCP bridge owned by the extint specialist: OpenAI Codex can run AS an MCP server over stdio (codex mcp-server), exposing itself to other agents/tools [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §5]. This KB issues a disciplined prompt to that bridge and receives an image; it does NOT own the MCP wiring, auth or secrets (extint does). The EXACT image-generation model reachable behind the bridge is [UNKNOWN] — the recon documents Codex as an MCP client/server but not which image model it fronts — so it must NOT be hard-coded or named speculatively; [METHOD] confirm the bridged generator by inspecting extint's Codex MCP server config and the tool it exposes before pinning any model name. Until confirmed, treat the generator as an interchangeable backend behind a stable prompt contract.

the UNKNOWN exact generator model and the METHOD to confirm it
treating the backend as interchangeable behind a stable prompt contract
excluded: extint's MCP wiring, auth and secrets

coupling prompts to an assumed generator's quirks before confirming it

nodes.definition: Define the structured-prompt discipline that turns a design intent into a generation request. Every prompt names, in order: the VIEW or framing (e.g. lateral, occlusal), the STRUCTURES to depict, the LABEL policy (which labels, or none for overlay), the STYLE register (line diagram vs shaded illustration, deck palette), and NEGATIVE constraints (no invented structures, no text unless specified, no decorative background) [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; standard prompt-engineering practice for controllable image generation]. A disciplined prompt is reproducible and diffable, so a re-prompt after a rejection changes exactly one controlled field. This discipline is the lever that makes generative output verifiable rather than a slot machine, and it is required before the anatomy constraints and style consistency can bite.

included: the view/structures/labels/style/negative prompt template
reproducible, diffable single-field re-prompts
prompt discipline as the precondition for accuracy and style control

pros.claim: A fixed prompt template makes generations reproducible and re-prompts precise, one controlled field at a time
pros.example: changing only the VIEW field from occlusal to lateral while holding structures, labels and style fixed

cons.claim: Rigid templates can under-specify for an unusual image and need per-case extension
cons.example: a composite figure that the five-field template cannot fully describe

failure_modes: free-text prompts that cannot be reproduced or diffed on a re-prompt
omitting negative constraints so the generator adds decorative or invented content
acceptance_tests: the discipline gives the view/structures/labels/style/negative template, makes re-prompts single-field and diffable, and is named the precondition for accuracy and style control
revisit_triggers: prompts routinely need per-case extension
a generator change alters which fields it honors
re-prompts stop being reproducible

base.update_signal: a generator change or recurring template under-specification revises the discipline

nodes.definition: Add the anatomy- and clinically-specific constraints that a structured prompt must carry when depicting the body. Constrain the COUNT of structures (e.g. the correct number of roots or cusps), the SPATIAL RELATIONS (which structure is medial/distal/superior to which), and the IDENTITY (correct named structures, no plausible-looking invented ones), and explicitly forbid the generator from 'improving' anatomy toward a prettier but wrong arrangement [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; the tendency of generative models to hallucinate anatomically impossible structures is a well-observed SIGNAL]. These constraints reduce but never eliminate error, which is exactly why the human clinical gate downstream is mandatory: prompt discipline lowers the hallucination rate, it does not certify truth.

included: structure-count, spatial-relation and identity constraints
forbidding invented or 'beautified' anatomy
framing constraints as risk-reduction not certification
excluded: the human clinical gate that certifies truth (downstream)

pros.claim: Explicit count and spatial constraints cut the most common anatomical hallucinations at the prompt stage
pros.example: pinning 'mandibular first molar, two roots, five cusps' so the generator cannot add a third root

cons.claim: Constraints reduce but cannot guarantee accuracy, and over-constraining can make the generator fail or distort
cons.example: so many pinned constraints that the generator produces a stiff, unusable image

failure_modes: treating prompt constraints as a substitute for the human clinical gate
under-constraining and letting the generator invent plausible-but-wrong structures
acceptance_tests: the node gives count, spatial-relation and identity constraints, forbids invented anatomy, and states constraints reduce risk but do not certify truth
revisit_triggers: a hallucination pattern recurs past the constraints
the generator changes and honors constraints differently
the clinical gate reports a constraint that should have caught an error

base.update_signal: a recurring hallucination or a generator change revises the constraints

nodes.definition: Enforce visual style consistency across a deck so images read as one coherent set rather than a patchwork. Pin a deck-level style register in every prompt — the same line-vs-shaded convention, colour palette, label typography and background treatment — because inconsistent styles across cards add extraneous variation that the coherence principle warns against and make the deck feel unreliable [ESTIMATE — design synthesis grounded in the coherence/consistency reasoning]. Consistency also aids the 3-image pattern: three views or frames of one concept must share a style to be read as a set. Style is a controlled field in the prompt template, versioned per deck so a style change is deliberate and re-appliable.

included: a pinned deck-level style register in every prompt
why inconsistency adds extraneous variation
style as a versioned controlled prompt field

pros.claim: A pinned deck style makes a set of cards read as one coherent resource and eases the 3-image grouping
pros.example: three views of a tooth sharing identical line weight and palette so they read as one object

cons.claim: A strict deck style can force a suboptimal register onto a concept that a different style would teach better
cons.example: a flat line style pinned deck-wide where a shaded render would show depth better

failure_modes: letting each card drift to its own style and fragmenting the deck
pinning a style so tightly it hurts a concept that needs a different register
acceptance_tests: the node pins a deck-level style register in the prompt, explains the extraneous-variation cost of inconsistency, and versions style as a controlled field
revisit_triggers: a deck's style is deliberately revised
a concept clearly needs a different register
learners report the deck as visually incoherent

base.update_signal: a deliberate style revision or an incoherence report changes the policy

nodes.definition: Define the owner's 3-images-per-concept pattern, the organizing convention for this KB's output. For each concept, produce THREE images in one of two variants: (a) three VIEWS — front / back / side — of a spatial structure, used when the learning objective is 3D form and orientation; or (b) three STORY FRAMES — a short before/during/after or step-1/2/3 sequence — used when the objective is a process or mechanism [FACT — the 3-images-per-concept front/back/side-or-story-frames pattern is the owner's stated want; the choice rule is ESTIMATE design synthesis]. The choice rule: pick views when the concept is a THING with spatial extent, story frames when it is a HAPPENING with temporal order. The view variant is deliberately shaped to double as the 3D pipeline's multiview input.

included: three views vs three story frames as the two variants
the thing-vs-happening choice rule

nodes.definition: Design the story-frame variant of the 3-image pattern for processes. Three frames tell one mechanism as a segmented sequence — e.g. frame 1 baseline, frame 2 the key change, frame 3 the outcome — with each frame a discrete chunk (segmenting) and visual continuity across frames (same viewpoint, style and characters so only the changing element moves) [ESTIMATE — design synthesis from the segmenting and coherence principles]. Story frames suit temporal or causal concepts a single static image cannot show, and they must maintain the same clinical accuracy and style discipline as any other image. The sequence's correctness — that the depicted progression is clinically true — is subject to the human gate exactly like a labeled diagram.

nodes.definition: Grade every generated image into a quality band before it approaches the clinical gate. Band A: ship-ready — legible at card size, labels correct and placed, structures plausibly accurate, style on-deck. Band B: fixable — a single controlled re-prompt would likely raise it to A (minor label or framing issue). Band C: reject — illegible, wrong structures, garbled text, or off-style enough that regeneration from scratch is warranted [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; band thresholds to be tuned against real output]. Banding is a fast triage on legibility and surface accuracy that routes images to ship, re-prompt, or discard; it is NOT the clinical certification, which only the human gate provides. The band and its reasons travel with the image into the gate and the regeneration loop.

nodes.definition: Enumerate the generative failure modes the bands and gate must catch, so review is systematic not ad hoc. The recurring classes: WRONG COUNT (extra or missing roots, cusps, chambers), FUSED or DUPLICATED anatomy (structures merged or repeated), IMPOSSIBLE ARRANGEMENT (anatomically invalid spatial relations), and GARBLED or INVENTED TEXT (misspelled, nonsense, or fabricated labels the prompt never asked for) [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; these are widely observed generative-image error classes and a known SIGNAL, to source-verify]. Each maps to a concrete check: count structures, look for fusion, verify spatial relations against the constraint, and read every label character by character. This catalog is the checklist the clinical gate runs and the reason banding alone is insufficient.

nodes.definition: Define the mandatory human clinical-correctness gate — the load-bearing safety mechanism of this KB. No anatomical or clinical image is attached to a shippable card until a human with the relevant knowledge verifies structure identity, count, and arrangement against the checklist of failure modes, because a generative model cannot certify its own output as clinically true [ESTIMATE — design decision; grounded in the fact that generated media hallucinates and the app teaches licensure-exam clinical content]. The gate's rule is absolute: UNVERIFIED ANATOMY NEVER SHIPS. A band-A image is a candidate for the gate, not a pass; the gate can fail a beautiful image and pass a plain one. Gate outcome (pass / fail-with-reasons) is recorded as provenance and travels with the asset.

nodes.definition: Define what happens to a rejected image: a bounded regenerate loop, not an infinite retry. A band-B or gate-failed image is re-prompted by changing exactly the one controlled field the reason names (label, view, count), regenerated, re-banded and re-gated; if it fails after a small bounded number of attempts (an ESTIMATE, e.g. ~3), it is ESCALATED to manual sourcing — a human-drawn diagram, a licensed reference image, or dropping the image and using text alone [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. The loop is bounded because generative retries have diminishing returns and can burn cost chasing an image the model cannot make; escalation to a non-generative source is a first-class outcome, not a failure. Every attempt's prompt and outcome is logged so the loop is diffable and the failure is diagnosable.

nodes.definition: Define what the producer hands downstream and how it is tagged honestly. Every delivered asset carries PROVENANCE: that it is machine-generated, the exact prompt used, the generator model IF known (else marked UNKNOWN, never guessed), the quality band, and the clinical-gate outcome (verified-by-whom or not-verified) [FACT — the honesty-tagging discipline is a house rule; the specific fields are design synthesis]. Occlusion source images go to contenteng with their maskable-region notes; view sets go to the neighboring 3D KB as multiview input; single diagrams and story frames attach to their cards. The contract's core promise is that no consumer can mistake a generated image for a human-verified clinical reference: the honesty tag travels with the pixels, and an un-gated asset is marked not-for-clinical-use.

nodes.definition: Compose the go/no-go this KB builds toward. GO: produce only pedagogical (coherence-passing, non-decorative) images in the three roles — occlusion sources, labeled diagrams, mechanism flowcharts — organized in the owner's 3-image pattern (views or story frames), generated through the extint-owned Codex MCP bridge under structured prompt discipline with anatomical-accuracy constraints and deck style consistency, triaged by quality bands, and cleared by a mandatory human clinical gate with a bounded regeneration-then-escalate loop, every asset handed off with honest provenance. NO-GO: do NOT ship decorative images, do NOT ship unverified anatomy, do NOT hard-code an unconfirmed generator model, and do NOT absorb contenteng's occlusion, the 3D pipeline, or extint's MCP wiring. An image earns a place on a card only when it teaches, is style-consistent, and is human-verified for clinical truth.

dominance_rules.rule: View consistency dominates per-image optimization for a 3D-bound set
dominance_rules.rationale: inconsistent scale or lighting across views degrades multiview 3D reconstruction
dominance_rules.trigger: a spatial concept's views will feed the 3D hand-off
dominance_rules.action: pin identical scale, lighting and style across the front/back/side set

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the coherence gate before requesting any generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating and reviewing decorative images that should never have been made

anti_rework_rules.rule: Select the image role before designing the layout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: producing an image the target card type cannot use and redoing it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the deck style register before generating a set of cards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a patchwork deck that must be regenerated card-by-card for consistency

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin anatomical counts and relations in the prompt before generating
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a batch of confidently-wrong anatomy that the gate rejects wholesale

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prefer deterministic label overlay before relying on generated text
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-generating images whose free-drawn labels are misspelled or invented

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the Codex-bridged generator with extint before pinning a model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: prompt tuning and provenance built on a fabricated model name that must be ripped out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the regeneration attempt cap before starting the loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unbounded retries that burn cost before anyone escalates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Constrain the three views to a shared register when a set is 3D-bound
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating an entire view set after a failed multiview reconstruction

iteration_protocol.trigger: extint confirms which image model the Codex MCP bridge fronts
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN generator field, update prompt tuning for the model's known limits, and re-check provenance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a wrong-anatomy image slips past the clinical gate into a shipped card
iteration_protocol.action: extend the failure-mode checklist and tighten the gate procedure

iteration_protocol.trigger: the multimedia-learning citations are source-verified in the L1 research pass
iteration_protocol.action: update the principle thresholds and any layout rules derived from them

iteration_protocol.trigger: the regeneration attempt cap proves mis-set (giving up too early or too late)
iteration_protocol.action: retune the cap and the escalation threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: Tripo changes its multiview input contract or a reconstruction fails on view inconsistency
iteration_protocol.action: adjust the view-set consistency requirements at the 3D hand-off

iteration_protocol.trigger: a consumer is found dropping provenance so a generated image is taken as verified
iteration_protocol.action: harden the hand-off contract and the not-for-clinical-use flagging

iteration_protocol.trigger: the deck style is deliberately revised or a concept needs an exception register
iteration_protocol.action: version the style change and re-apply it across the affected set

priority_rationale: The scope frame and coherence gate come first because they decide whether an image is produced at all and keep decorative requests out of the pipeline; the role taxonomy and multimedia principles come next as the design foundation that fixes layout, maskability and label rules; the Codex bridge and endpoint options establish the generation transport with its UNKNOWN backend held honestly; prompt discipline, anatomy constraints and style consistency turn design intent into verifiable generation requests; the 3-image pattern, multiview hand-off and story-frame sequence organize output in the owner's convention with a clean 3D on-ramp; and the quality bands, hallucination catalog, human clinical gate, bounded regeneration loop, hand-off contract and production verdict come last because they compose every upstream step into a triaged, human-verified, honestly-tagged pipeline whose absolute rule is that no decorative image and no unverified anatomy ever ships.
